name: Cinnamon Roll Apple Pie
desc: Canned apple pie filling in a store-bought crust, topped with slices of a cinnamon-swirled pie dough log.

source.title: Cinnamon Roll Apple Pie
source.evidence: Same two 540 ml (18.9 oz) cans of E.D. Smith apple pie filling, a buttered cinnamon-sugar pie dough log sliced over the top, egg wash with turbinado sugar, and a 400°F then 350°F bake.

ingredients.raw: 2 (9 in) pie crusts, store-bought refrigerated or homemade
Butter or baking spray, for the pie plate
2 (540 ml / 18.9 oz) cans E.D. Smith apple pie filling
1 large egg, beaten, for egg wash

steps: Grease a 9 in glass or ceramic pie plate. On a lightly floured surface, roll one crust into a 12 in circle, fit it into the plate, and crimp the edge. Prick the bottom and sides with a fork and refrigerate.
Roll the second crust into a rough 10x12 in rectangle. Brush with the melted butter and sprinkle the cinnamon and brown sugar all the way to the edges.
Starting at a long edge, roll it up tightly into a log and pinch the seam. Refrigerate until firm, about 30 min.
Slice the log into 1/4 in rounds.
Fill the chilled crust with the apple pie filling and arrange the rounds over the top, slightly overlapping. Refrigerate 30 min, until the topping is firm. Meanwhile heat the oven to 400°F.
Brush the crust edge and the rounds with egg wash and sprinkle with turbinado sugar.
Bake 15 min at 400°F, then lower to 350°F and bake 40-45 min more, until the filling bubbles and the crust is deep golden brown. If the edges brown too fast, cover them loosely with foil.
Cool completely on a rack, at least 2 hr, before slicing.
tips: Olive & Mango's version uses 1/2 cup brown sugar and 2 tsp cinnamon for the swirl, a third crust for a fuller topping, and bakes 20 min at 400°F then 45-60 min at 350°F. This one is heavier on cinnamon and lighter on sugar.
Bake any leftover rounds on a parchment-lined sheet at 400°F until golden and crisp, about 12 min.
